Kidzoi Enables Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory Activity and Variant Effect Prediction in Kidney.

Kidzoi is a kidney-specific sequence-to-function deep learning model created by transfer learning from the pretrained Borzoi model using single-nucleus chromatin accessibility data. It enables cell-type-specific prediction of regulatory activity and variant effects in the kidney, addressing the limitation that no single pretrained model covers all cell types and conditions. This provides a practical template for adapting general S2F models to specialized tissues without training from scratch.

Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.

This study builds a prognostic model for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes linked to 'floatptosis,' a newly described form of vacuolar cell death triggered by outer membrane vesicles from a Bergeyella cardium variant. By integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data, the authors link floatptosis-related gene expression to patient survival and immunotherapy-related features. The work is exploratory and the clinical utility of the model remains to be validated.

Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.

This study identifies cellular senescence-associated gene signatures through pan-cancer screening and builds a prognostic risk model for bladder urothelial carcinoma that integrates multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signals to tumor microenvironment features, offering a framework for molecular risk assessment in BLCA.

PoolParty: streamlined design of DNA sequence libraries in Python.

PoolParty is a new Python package that streamlines the design of DNA sequence libraries used in massively parallel reporter assays, deep mutational scanning, and other multiplex assays of variant effect. It addresses the lack of purpose-built software, which has made library design tedious and error-prone, and can also support in silico analysis of genomic AI models.

Assessing the predictive potential of the Holstein bovine sperm methylome for bull fertility using machine learning.

This study tested whether DNA methylation patterns in Holstein bull sperm can predict bull fertility using machine learning models. Leveraging existing methylation data, the authors evaluated the predictive potential of sperm methylome features for fertility outcomes, though the abstract does not report specific performance results. The work represents an initial step toward developing operational epigenetic biomarkers for male fertility in dairy cattle.

Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data.

The authors present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL), a free, community-supported web platform that bundles over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows for reproducible, FAIR analysis of microbial omics data. It aims to lower computational and technical barriers for microbiologists working with metabarcoding, metagenomic, and metatranscriptomic data. The platform is backed by the Galaxy ecosystem and global microbiology communities.

Experimental benchmarking of in silico annotations at prostate cancer risk loci and hypothesis-generating cross-cancer prioritisation of ovarian risk variants.

The authors re-analyzed a massively parallel reporter assay (DiR-seq) testing 208 prostate cancer risk SNPs across three cell lines, identifying 50 regulatory SNPs under FDR control. They then benchmarked standard in silico annotation tools against these experimental results and used the findings to prioritize ovarian cancer risk variants by cross-cancer analogy. The work provides an experimental reference set for evaluating computational regulatory variant predictions.

Ultra-sensitive Mapping of Cell-free DNA-derived Methylomes Reveals Brain-specific Epigenetic Alterations Implicated in Alzheimer's Disease.

The authors applied LABS, an ultra-sensitive linear amplification-based whole-genome bisulfite sequencing method, to profile methylation in serum-derived cell-free DNA from age- and sex-matched pathologically confirmed Alzheimer's disease cases and non-AD controls from the Rush Memory and Aging Project. They detected altered methylation features in cfDNA that appear to reflect brain-specific epigenetic changes associated with AD. This demonstrates the feasibility of using low-input cfDNA methylomes as a minimally invasive window into AD-related brain epigenetics.

Agent_K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery.

Agent_K is an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the entire workflow from bacterial whole-genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) identification, pathway mapping, and candidate metabolite discovery. It addresses the fragmentation of existing computational tools by integrating data processing, annotation, and analysis across heterogeneous platforms with minimal manual intervention. This enables more streamlined genome-guided natural product discovery.

Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk.

The authors present Torino, a computational framework that discovers RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA sequencing data without relying on existing transcript annotations. By adapting non-negative matrix factorization to model coverage variation across samples, Torino identifies unannotated RNA processing events and links them to disease risk across tissues, individuals, and disease states. This reference-free approach reveals disease-relevant isoform changes that conventional annotation-based methods miss.

SLCNV is a Nextflow-based pipeline that streamlines copy number variation analysis from low-pass whole genome sequencing data, addressing the need for user-friendly tools that don't require extensive computational expertise. It enables wet-lab biologists to perform multiple copy number-related analyses in a flexible workflow.

Viscous mechanical cues encode metastatic behavior through cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling.

This preprint shows that the viscosity of a tumor's mechanical environment, not just its stiffness, can drive metastatic-like behavior in cancer cells. Cells grown on soft but viscous substrates developed stiffness-associated traits such as increased intrinsic stiffness, nuclear YAP accumulation, and enhanced migration through narrow constrictions, with accompanying epigenomic and transcriptomic changes linked to cytoskeletal-nuclear coupling and chromatin remodeling. The work suggests viscosity is an underappreciated mechanical cue that cancer cells decode to adopt aggressive phenotypes.

Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.

By integrating Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical prostate samples spanning benign, primary, and castration-resistant cancer, the authors mapped A/B chromatin compartment shifts while correcting for copy number variation and tumor purity. They found that compartment shifts recur in prostate cancer and are linked to epigenetic reprogramming, suggesting 3D genome reorganization contributes to disease progression.

Catalytic DNA for Precision Diagnostics: DNAzyme-Based Approaches to Single-Nucleotide Polymorphism Detection.

This review examines DNAzyme-based biosensors for detecting single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), the most common form of human genetic variation and key biomarkers for disease risk and precision medicine. The authors argue that these catalytic nucleic acid sensors offer advantages over conventional genotyping methods by combining programmable sequence recognition with isothermal catalytic signal amplification, enabling sensitive SNP detection in complex biological samples without sophisticated instrumentation.

Ultrafast alignment-free detection of viral genome variation with bronko.

The authors present bronko, an alignment-free framework that detects viral genome variation directly from sequencing reads without aligning them to a reference. It uses locality-sensitive bucketing and k-mer counting to rapidly identify SNPs, enabling scalable analysis of massive viral sequencing datasets that would be computationally prohibitive for traditional alignment-based pipelines.

O-acetylation mediates four distinct structural variants of the pneumococcal vaccine serotype 15A capsule polysaccharide.

This study re-examined serogroup 15 pneumococcal capsule polysaccharides and found that O-acetylation generates four distinct structural variants of the vaccine serotype 15A capsule, rather than the single non-acetylated form and one acetylated counterpart (15F) previously recognized. The work shows that conventional serological and molecular typing can miss O-acetylation differences, which matters because 15A is included in newer conjugate vaccines and such variants could affect vaccine coverage and immune recognition.

Proteomics-Guided Discovery of Candidate Enzymes for Degradation of a Rare Pyruvylated Glycosaminogalactan by a Newly Isolated Luteolibacter Strain.

The authors isolated a new Luteolibacter strain capable of degrading EPSLp, a high-molecular-mass glycosaminogalactan from Lactiplantibacillus pentosus that contains an uncommon pyruvylated GalNAc-Gal motif. Using proteomics-guided analysis of the strain's expressed enzymes, they identified candidate CAZymes responsible for degrading this rare exopolysaccharide structure. This work expands knowledge of carbohydrate-active enzyme diversity and provides leads for degrading non-canonical EPS modifications.

Conservative evolution of genetic and features in Caenorhabditis becei, an experimentally tractable gonochoristic worm.

The authors identify Caenorhabditis becei, a gonochoristic (male/female) nematode, as an experimentally tractable model for evolutionary genetics outside the well-studied self-fertile Elegans Group. They show that transmission-genetic properties known from androdioecious Elegans Group species are conserved in this Japonica Group species, despite its obligate outcrossing lifestyle. This expands the Caenorhabditis toolkit to a more representative reproductive mode for the genus.

CALB1 expression in meningioma: associations with progression-free survival and chromosome arm 6q loss.

This study examined calbindin D28K (CALB1) protein expression in 231 meningioma tissue samples from 147 patients and found associations between CALB1 expression, progression-free survival, and loss of chromosome arm 6q. Large language and foundation models in predictive plant breeding: Capabilities, evidence, and challenges.

A recall-rescue fuzzy layer over paired Z-DNA Hunter scans for fast Z-DNA detection.

The authors present Z-DNA-Fuzzy Hunter 1.1.0, a tool that improves Z-DNA-forming region detection by combining a permissive scan (high recall) with a stringent scan (high precision) and integrating their outputs through a fuzzy expert layer. This dual-scan recall-rescue strategy addresses the sensitivity-specificity trade-off in sequence-based Z-DNA prediction while remaining fast and interpretable.

Inferring causal networks for genomic trios with high-dimensional confounding variables.

The paper introduces a new method for inferring causal relationships between molecular phenotypes (like gene expression) using genetic variants as instruments under the principle of Mendelian randomization, specifically designed to handle high-dimensional confounding variables such as other genes, processes, and demographic factors. Existing methods struggle with such high-dimensional confounders, and this work aims to robustly account for them in causal network inference for genomic trio data.

SCCmecExtractor: a tool for extracting staphylococcal cassette chromosome elements from whole-genome sequences.

SCCmecExtractor is a lightweight Python toolkit that identifies and extracts complete staphylococcal cassette chromosome (SCC) elements from whole-genome assemblies by matching degenerate attachment site (att) patterns. Unlike existing SCCmec typing tools, it can extract the full element sequence and classify SCC elements that lack methicillin resistance genes. This fills a gap for studying the diversity and mobility of these important mobile genetic elements.

The Promise and Limitations of Metabolic Trait Prediction Across Diverse Bacteria.

This study tests whether metabolic traits like substrate utilization can be reliably predicted from bacterial genomes alone by comparing four common bioinformatic tools against high-throughput growth phenotypes of 186 marine bacteria. It finds that for simple substrates, prediction accuracy is limited and varies widely across taxa and substrates, challenging the assumption that genome-based inference is reliable. The work highlights important limitations of current metabolic prediction tools and the need for caution when using them for diverse bacteria.

Long-read sequencing of FLG identifies extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and detects rare loss-of-function variants.

This study uses long-read sequencing to overcome the difficulty of characterizing the highly repetitive exon 3 of the FLG gene, which encodes filaggrin and harbors loss-of-function variants that predispose to atopic dermatitis. By sequencing 192 samples from Belgium, Ireland, and Rwanda, the authors uncovered extensive copy number variation in exon 3 and identified both common and rare loss-of-function variants associated with atopic dermatitis. The work demonstrates that long-read technology substantially improves variant detection in this clinically important but technically challenging gene.

ogMapper improves speed and memory for short-sequencing read mapping using a novel guided sparse genome index.

ogMapper introduces a novel guided sparse genome indexing strategy for short-read mapping that reduces the memory required for the genome index to a factor β commonly around 0.5, compared to β ≈ 10 for bwa-mem2 and β ≈ 1.9 for minimap2. The approach improves speed and memory efficiency for everyday short-read sequencing applications.
